title: A coding harness lifted Opus 5 by 66 points on the same weights - TCR 08/15/26
description:
Claude Opus 5 jumped from 30.2% to 96.2% on ARC-AGI-3 with nothing but a stock coding harness, OpenAI's Cerebras-powered Ultrafast tier ran GPT-5.6 Sol at 750 tokens per second, and Georgia Power extended the commission's review period for the 25-year contract behind OpenAI's $20 billion data center after regulators pressed on its 3.2-gigawatt power request.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-august-15-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:41 The frontier compresses on speed and scaffolding
4:23 Georgia Power delays the OpenAI data-center deal
6:48 FDA clears a new myeloma drug class
9:26 Apple and Alibaba co-build a China model
12:00 The labor signal sharpens and retraining pilots land
15:02 Close

This episode covers the frontier compressing on speed and agentic scaffolding, Gemini 3.7 Flash, which Google says costs half as much as the prior version, the Georgia Power ratepayer-transparency fight, the FDA's accelerated approval of Bristol's Zenbexus myeloma drug for certain patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma against a stricter remission measure, Apple and Alibaba co-training a China-market model, and the Richmond Fed's finding that AI-exposed workers are re-entering jobs more slowly.

On August 13 the frontier moved on two axes at once. Opus 5, handed only a stock coding harness, leapt 66 points on ARC-AGI-3 and resolved nine ProgramBench tasks, and news reports said a neurosurgery resident used a sixteen-hour AI run to produce a solution to a two-decade math conjecture. The gains came from the scaffolding, cheap and portable enough to have lifted several capable models tested with it, while GPT-5.6 Sol ran 14 times faster on Cerebras wafers and Gemini 3.7 Flash arrived at what Google says is half the prior price. The real constraint moved off the chip: OpenAI's $20 billion Georgia campus, projected to draw three times Atlanta's electricity, entered extended commission review after the Public Service Commission objected to a fully redacted 25-year power contract, and advocates asked for disclosure, a standard tariff class for very large loads, and a public vote for anything above 500 megawatts. The FDA granted accelerated approval to Bristol's Zenbexus for certain patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, a new oral myeloma class measured against a finer remission test that resets the bar for the whole field, Apple co-built a China model with Alibaba across a border policy tries to seal, and the Richmond Fed found job-finding rates fell 13 points for strongly-attached workers in AI-exposed roles as the UK launched three-week retraining boot camps.
